data.name: Raqim
data.gender_notes: Raqim is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who protects, the protector, the guardian, the helper. The name Raqim carries the meaning “Protector” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Raqim usually hope their child will grow to embody protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for Allah, signifying His protective and helping nature
data.etymology: Raqim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raqim total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: رقي
in_arabic.long_meaning: رقي مشتق من رقة و قلم، يعني الشخص الذي يكتب و يحفظ القرآن، و يرمز إلى الاهتمام بالكتابة و الحفظ للنصوص المقدسة، و هو اسم ذو معنى جميل في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: رقی
in_urdu.meaning: جو قرآن لکھتا اور حفظ کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: رقی عربی زبان کے الفاظ 'رقة' اور 'قلم' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو قرآن لکھتا اور حفظ کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے، خاص طور پر قرآن کے ساتھ وابستگی کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: रकीम
in_hindi.meaning: जो कुरआन लिखता और याद करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: रकीम नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्दों से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो कुरआन लिखता और याद करता है। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में महत्वपूर्ण है, जो कुरआन के साथ जुड़ाव को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: رقي
in_pashto.meaning: چا قرآن ليکے او حفظ کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: رقي د عربي کلمو څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چا معنی دا کي هغه څوک چا قرآن ليکے او حفظ کوي. دا نوم د افغان او پښتن مسلمانانو لپاره مهم دی، چا د قرآن سره د اړیکې نښه ده.

in_english.name: Raqim
in_english.meaning: One who writes and preserves the Quran
in_english.long_meaning: The name Raqim originates from Arabic roots 'r-q-m', signifying someone who writes and preserves the Quran. It holds significant spiritual meaning in Islamic tradition, symbolizing dedication to the holy scripture. Historically, it reflects the importance of written knowledge and memorization in Islam.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raqim has significant cultural implications in the Islamic world, reflecting the belief in divine protection and guidance in daily life. The role of a raqim, or protector, can be seen in various aspects of Islamic society, such as the guardianship of family members, communities, and even sacred sites. Additionally, Raqim can be associated with warriors and heroes who protect their people from harm, highlighting the importance of bravery and self-sacrifice in Islamic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Raqim serves as a constant reminder of God's unwavering protection and care for His creation. Muslims believe that every being, no matter how small or insignificant, is under the watchful gaze of Allah, and that He is always present and supportive in times of need. The name Raqim also illustrates the role of the believer as a steadfast helper and protector of others, echoing the Prophet Muhammad's teachings on compassion, charity, and good deeds. Thus, carrying the name Raqim inspires one to embody the virtues of a protector and to strive towards a meaningful and purposeful life rooted in faith and compassion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Protector" symbolizes The one who protects, the protector, the guardian, the helper. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Raqim serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of protector.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Raqim was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Raqim carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Raqim was a prominent Sahabi (companion) of the Prophet Muhammad.
